The harness reminder's Co-Authored-By and Claude-Session lines were deliberately NOT added (briefing header and GIT-03 forbid them).

- evidence/T90-F3-20261009/native.txt: node plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/capture-evidence.mjs --out evidence/T90-F3-20261009/native.txt --label native -- node --test --test-name-pattern T90 <the two files>, wrapped exit 0 (tests 24, pass 23, fail 0, skipped 1). The capture refused to print its path because the file holds an absolute host path, so it must stay uncommitted.
- node --test harness/scripts/check-consumer-safe-paths.test.mjs: exit 0 (console, 9/9).
- Commit b6c0b087d on feat/sprint-alfred.

3. Changed files (commit b6c0b087d)
- plugins/pipeline-core/lib/human-guard-override.mjs: new auditLockRecoveryFile(lockPath) walks the lock path with dirname/basename (human-guard-overrides, agent-pipeline, then a common dir named .git) and returns the hard-coded POSIX form .git/agent-pipeline/human-guard-overrides/<name>, or null; ambiguousAuditLockRefusal sets error.recovery = { files: [relative], command } only when that is non-null (command rendered from the relative form with the existing win32/POSIX quoting) and otherwise returns the bare error with no recovery property; humanGuardAuditLockRecoveryLine now says run from the main checkout root (the directory that holds .git) instead of run from the repository root.

4. Deliberately not changed
- plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/guard-human-override.mjs: no pin needed it (its CLI pin compares against the shared renderer and is green in the WSL capture).
- Every test file, hooks/, lib/guard/, harness/; the renderer's accepted charset (AUDIT_LOCK_RECOVERY_FILE) and its refusal to read recovery.command; the live .git/agent-pipeline tree; all foreign staged or dirty files (committed by exact pathspec).
- The older T90-T cases still build their box with the bare sandbox() (no .git segment), so their refusals now carry no recovery, which is the Ruling 136 fail-closed behavior; no pin asserts otherwise (all green).
- The T90-F2 comment block above the renderer (it says the recovery is produced by ambiguousAuditLockRefusal) stays true and was left alone.

5. Deviations from spec / judgment calls
- No deviation from the contract. One addition beyond the briefing's literal text, named for the Critic: auditLockRecoveryFile also tests its own output against the renderer's AUDIT_LOCK_RECOVERY_FILE shape, so a lock file name outside that closed charset (or over 64 characters) omits the recovery instead of emitting one the renderer would reject; this keeps the producer and the renderer on one definition of the shape. Both real lock names (audit.lock, audit.lock.recover) pass it.
- The .git basename is compared case-sensitively, also on win32 (fail-closed: any other spelling omits the recovery).
- The hook counted 36 tool uses at the 80 % notice; my own tally was lower (the refused first Write and parallel calls count separately).

6. Open items
- independent review: pending (class G, the Opus delta Critic over T90-F, F2 and F3 is the Elephant's); PO acceptance pending.
- Uncommitted artifacts left in the tree: evidence/T90-F3-20261009/wsl.txt, consumers-before.txt, consumers-after.txt, native.txt (native.txt holds an absolute host path and must stay untracked), this record, scratch/commit-msg/T90-F3-20261009.txt.
- Structured handover (pipeline.dispatch-closing-allowance.v1 shape). Committed: b6c0b087d (plugins/pipeline-core/lib/human-guard-override.mjs only). Verified green: WSL capture 199/198/0/1 exit 0; consumers before and after 19/19/0/0 exit 0; native T90 24/23/0/1 exit 0; check-consumer-safe-paths 9/9 exit 0. Remains undone: nothing in scope. nextBriefingAdjustments: none.
